question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

She quickly climbed onto her upper _______ to give a wide _______ to the unruly family creating a scene below.
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. berth, berth .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires two homonyms that make sense in the context.
 
• In the first blank, the word **"berth"** refers to a bed or bunk, typically on a train or ship.
 
• In the second blank, the word **"berth"** also means giving space or distance, as in "giving a wide berth."
 
• The pair **"berth, berth"** fits perfectly in the sentence.

Correct sentence: *She quickly climbed onto her upper **berth** to give a wide **berth** to the unruly family creating a scene below*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homonyms:** Words that sound the same (or are spelled the same) but have different meanings.
 
• **Examples:** 
 
 
• **"Berth" (a sleeping space) and "berth" (space or distance).**
 
• **"Bank" (a financial institution) and "bank" (the side of a river).**
